sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.4
sources.evidence: The March 5, 2026 announcement releases GPT-5.4 in ChatGPT as GPT-5.4 Thinking, the API as gpt-5.4, and Codex. It explicitly describes reasoning, coding, vision, tool calling and native computer use. API/Codex support up to 1M context, while ChatGPT retained its prior limits and Codex initially offered long context experimentally.

sources.title: GPT-5.4 API model documentation
sources.evidence: The exact current model record identifies default snapshot gpt-5.4-2026-03-05, text/image input, text output, 1,050,000 context, 128,000 maximum output, reasoning efforts none through xhigh, Chat Completions and Responses, function calling, file uploads, computer use and explicit prompt caching. No numerical parameter count is disclosed.

sources.title: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card
sources.evidence: The original card identifies GPT-5.4 Thinking as the reasoning model, describes data and reinforcement-learning training in section 2, and reports safety/capability evaluations. Its complete extracted text supplies no numerical production parameter count or detailed network architecture. The later mini appendix is a separate variant, not a size disclosure for GPT-5.4.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: The later April 23, 2026 card includes explicit GPT-5.4 Thinking comparison columns for safety, health, cyber, monitorability and other evaluations. It uses latest prior-model versions. Those columns and related discussion report performance and response lengths, not total/active production parameters or GPT-5.4 neural block structure.

sources.title: Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL
sources.evidence: May 7, 2026 research explicitly names released GPT-5.4 Thinking among models affected by accidental CoT grading in RL. Its exact-model analysis recomputes usefulness rewards and examines monitorability, with no total/active parameter or structural architecture disclosure. GPT-5.4 Instant is separately discussed and is not treated as this model.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: The guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6 and describes OpenAI prompt caching using Transformer attention key/value projections. Combined with GPT-5.4 explicit caching support, it supports a qualified broad Transformer inference only, not dense/MoE topology or complete block composition.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: For vision-capable models, PDF input is processed into extracted text and page images. Responses supports PDF file input and Chat Completions accepts PDF files. This establishes an API document format when combined with the exact GPT-5.4 vision and endpoint support, not another native modality.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: The March 5, 2026 entry releases GPT-5.4 to Chat Completions and Responses. March 13 documents an image-encoder bug fix for GPT-5.4 image inputs. June 1 extends distribution to Amazon Bedrock with regional feature differences. These are service history, not separate original release dates.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The complete current page was checked for exact GPT-5.4 identifiers. It lists GPT-5.4 nano and GPT-5.4 Cyber notices but no shutdown notice for gpt-5.4 or gpt-5.4-2026-03-05. Sibling notices do not apply to this model, and documentation alone does not prove a live endpoint.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Section 9.1 reserves service intellectual-property rights and grants limited service use rather than ownership. Together with the exact hosted release, this supports a descriptive proprietary classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI model inventory
sources.evidence: The inventory lists GPT-5.4 among hosted models. Its separate Open-weight section lists gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b with Apache 2.0. The checked exact release and documentation provide no downloadable GPT-5.4 weights.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-5.4 record
sources.evidence: The original catalog lead was inspected from its current raw file. Its generic family and promotional description were not treated as primary evidence; its context and modality claims were checked independently.

name.note: Official API display name; GPT-5.4 Thinking is the corresponding ChatGPT name.

developer.note: Identified by the developer announcement and system card.

family.note: Normalize to the named GPT-5.4 generation. This does not imply shared weights with mini, nano, Pro or Instant.

release_date.note: Explicit public launch across ChatGPT, Codex and API. The March 13 encoder fix and June 1 additional provider availability do not move the original release date.

open_weights.note: Hosted model distribution under reserved service IP; checked official sources provide no downloadable weights for this model.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-service classification; not a claimed SPDX identifier or downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: No total production parameter count in the original card, later exact-model GPT-5.5 comparisons, current API record or exact-model RL research. Targeted first-party parameter, training and interpretability searches found no numerical disclosure. Benchmark scores, response lengths and sibling specifications are not model counts.

active_parameters_b.note: No per-token active count in the checked original and later exact-model evidence. Do not equate total and active or infer dense/MoE layout from inference behavior.

architecture.note: Qualified cross-source inference: exact GPT-5.4 documentation supports prompt caching, and OpenAI pre-GPT-5.6 caching documentation describes Transformer attention KV state. This is a broad classification only. Original/later cards and exact-model training/interpretability searches did not establish full block composition, dense/MoE topology or layer counts.

context_window.note: Exact API context is 1,050,000 tokens, with 128,000 maximum output. Do not derive an independent input ceiling by subtraction or substitute product-specific ChatGPT/Codex launch limits. Endpoint operation was not tested.

modalities.note: Text/image are native inputs and text is the output. PDF is retained as an API-supported input format converted into extracted text and page images. Hosted image-generation tool support does not establish native image output.

reasoning.note: Exact API documentation exposes reasoning tokens with none, low, medium, high and xhigh effort. The none default does not negate reasoning capability; the card and later RL research independently describe its internal reasoning training.

tool_call.note: Exact model documentation explicitly supports function calling and tools including computer use; not inferred from a sibling.

description.value: OpenAI reasoning model for coding and general tasks, with text and image input, tool calling and computer use.
description.note: Replace relative cost/performance promotion with supported purpose and interface capabilities.

sources.label: Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL

patch.notes: Released March 5, 2026 in ChatGPT as GPT-5.4 Thinking, Codex and the API; the API default snapshot is gpt-5.4-2026-03-05. The API context is 1,050,000 tokens with a 128,000-token maximum output; ChatGPT and Codex product limits differ. OpenAI documented an image-encoder fix on March 13. PDF means API extraction into text and page images, and hosted image generation is a tool rather than native model output. Transformer is a qualified broad inference from exact-model prompt caching support and OpenAI pre-GPT-5.6 KV-cache documentation. Detailed topology and total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed in the checked sources. No exact-model API shutdown notice was found in the current deprecation page; live endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Confirmed March 5 public release, exact API snapshot, 1.05M context, text/image/PDF input semantics, reasoning and tools. Corrected family, proprietary licensing, broad qualified Transformer classification and promotional description. Recorded the later encoder fix and product-specific context distinctions. Counts remain undisclosed after original, later comparison and exact-model training research checks.
